title: Korea’s leverage trap has an echo in India
summary: Indian brokers are lending large sums to retail investors, creating systemic risk.  Retail investors are borrowing heavily to buy stocks at stretched valuations.  This margin debt has ballooned significantly, with new-age brokers aggressively competing.  Unlike Korea's AI focus, India's debt supports stocks global investors are avoiding.  Policymakers face challenges as inflation and a weakening rupee test their resolve.

title: Sebi opens faster route for rollout of AIF plans
summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has introduced a new green channel mechanism. This new framework, called GARUDA, aims to speed up the launch of Alternative Investment Fund schemes. Regular AIF schemes can now be launched ten days after filing their placement memorandum. Accredited investor only funds and large value funds have been granted further flexibility. These changes will allow for quicker introduction of new AIF plans.

title: Sebi agrees to settle all NSE cases, clears way for mega IPO

The Securities and Exchange Board of India agreed to the settlement terms after years of legal battles. NSE plans to raise over twenty-six thousand crore rupees this year. The financial impact of the settlement has already been accounted for.

title: NSE Q1 profit up 8.7% at Rs 3,120 crore

Meanwhile, consolidated revenue from operations increased by 13% from the same period last year.
